## Definitions

- [statement] Tricolon is not proof of AI authorship: corporate communications, grant applications and student essays show the same habit, and prompting can remove the tell; the signal is cumulative with other tells. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-13) — https://www.cherryleaf.com/2026/02/indicators-that-suggest-something-was-written-by-ai/ · keywords: Tricolon and rule-of-three lists · also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing guide says LLMs overuse the rule of three in forms from adjective-adjective-adjective to short phrase, short phrase, and short phrase, often to make superficial analyses look more comprehensive. (medium confidence) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing · keywords: Tricolon and rule-of-three lists · also: https://www.cherryleaf.com/2026/02/indicators-that-suggest-something-was-written-by-ai/
- [statement] Proposed explanation: LLMs reproduce a technique that is effective in human rhetoric (e.g. 'I came, I saw, I conquered') but lack the judgment to hold back, so saturation dulls the effect. (medium confidence) — https://www.deadlanguagesociety.com/p/rhetorical-analysis-ai · keywords: Tricolon and rule-of-three lists · also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing
- [statement] Heuristic: if nearly every enumeration in a paragraph comes in threes, the text is likely AI output; humans break the pattern with two, four, or long lists. (medium confidence) — https://www.cherryleaf.com/2026/02/indicators-that-suggest-something-was-written-by-ai/ · keywords: Tricolon and rule-of-three lists · also: https://www.deadlanguagesociety.com/p/rhetorical-analysis-ai
